lessons.title: What Is Pressure? Measuring the Invisible Push — Shoes, Scales, and Force Per Unit Area

quiz.prompt: A sealed empty plastic jerrycan has had some air removed from inside and it is crumpling inwards. Which statement best describes how the air OUTSIDE is acting on it?
choices: It pushes only on the sides, because the top and bottom are flat
It pushes only downwards on the top of the jerrycan
It pushes inwards on every face: top, bottom and all four sides
It does not push at all; the plastic simply becomes weak
quiz.rationale: Atmospheric pressure acts on every exposed face of an object, so the outside air pushes inwards on all six faces. Students who draw arrows only on the top hold the 'downward only' misconception.
quiz.placement: Silent Force-Diagramming of the collapsed jerrycan

quiz.prompt: A teacher presses a flat textbook onto her palm, then presses a sharp pencil tip onto her palm with about the same force. The pencil feels much more painful. What is the best explanation?
choices: The book has a smaller area, so it spreads the force less
The force is about the same, but the pencil tip has a much smaller contact area, so the pressure is greater
The pencil is heavier than the book
The pencil tip pushes with a much bigger force than the book
quiz.rationale: Pressure is force divided by area (P = F/A). With the same force, a smaller contact area gives a larger pressure.
quiz.placement: Part A: Pencil vs. Book Demonstration

quiz.prompt: A student has a mass of 50 kg (g = 10 N/kg). She stands on one shoe whose sole has a contact area of 200 cm². Taking her weight as shared equally between both feet, what pressure does one shoe exert on the floor? (1 m² = 10,000 cm²)
quiz.rationale: Weight = 50 × 10 = 500 N, so one foot carries 250 N. Area = 200 ÷ 10,000 = 0.02 m². P = 250 ÷ 0.02 = 12,500 Pa.

quiz.prompt: Which choice correctly gives the definition of pressure and its SI unit?
choices: Pressure = area ÷ force; unit is the Newton (N)
Pressure = mass ÷ area; unit is the kilogram (kg)
Pressure = force × area; unit is the square metre (m²)
Pressure = force ÷ area; unit is the Pascal (Pa), which is N/m²
quiz.rationale: Pressure is force per unit area, P = F/A, measured in Pascals where 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Inverting the formula or using mass instead of force are common errors.
quiz.placement: Formal definition and note frame (P = F/A, unit Pascal)

quiz.prompt: A maize bag of mass 90 kg (g = 10 N/kg) is placed on a wooden pallet in a warehouse in Eldoret. The pallet has 4 legs, each with a base area of 25 cm². The weight is shared equally by the legs. What pressure does each leg exert on the floor? (1 m² = 10,000 cm²)
quiz.placement: Extension Problem 1: maize bag on a wooden pallet

quiz.prompt: A Maasai elder leans on a rungu whose handle tip has an area of 2 cm², with a force of 150 N. A nurse at Kenyatta National Hospital leans on a flat crutch base of area 50 cm² with the same 150 N force. How do the pressures on the floor compare?
choices: The rungu exerts 48 times more pressure than the crutch
The pressures are equal, because both forces are 150 N
The rungu exerts 25 times more pressure than the crutch
The crutch exerts 25 times more pressure than the rungu
quiz.rationale: Rungu: 150 ÷ 0.0002 = 750,000 Pa. Crutch: 150 ÷ 0.005 = 30,000 Pa. The ratio is 750,000 ÷ 30,000 = 25, so the crutch is safer for a soft floor.
quiz.placement: Extension Problem 2: rungu and crutch comparison

quiz.prompt: Which statement best describes atmospheric pressure?
choices: It is a force that acts only downwards on the top of objects
It is the weight of the column of air above a surface, and it acts on every exposed face of an object
It is the force of moving wind, and it acts only in the direction the wind blows
It is the pressure of the air trapped inside a container only
quiz.rationale: Atmospheric pressure comes from the weight of the air column above a surface and it pushes on all exposed faces, not just the top.
quiz.placement: Two-colour DQB cards: 'What do I now THINK is causing the jerrycan to crush?'

quiz.prompt: An empty sealed jerrycan with normal air inside and outside stays intact. After some air is pumped out of it, it collapses. Which explanation is correct?
choices: Before, there was no air pushing on the jerrycan at all
Before, the air pressure inside pushing outwards balanced the air pressure outside pushing inwards; after, the pressure inside was much less, so the outside pressure crushed it
The air outside became heavier after the air inside was removed
The plastic was already weak and only needed a small push from the pump
quiz.rationale: With equal pressure inside and outside the inward and outward pushes balance. Removing air lowers the inside pressure, so the unbalanced outside pressure collapses the jerrycan.
quiz.placement: Revised jerrycan model: sentence frame 'Before the air was removed... After air was removed...'
